subject: Tranche acceptance cadence & billing escrow for SkyBridge (GCP / Azure private offers)
messages:
From: Ian Choi <ian.choi@skybridge.io>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP request + procurement constraints for SkyBridge private offers

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency profile and cost controls. Procurement asked me to get a formal mutual action plan (MAP) for the private-offer path (we're evaluating both GCP and Azure marketplace private offers). Key asks from procurement:

- A staged acceptance schedule (technical acceptance -> production sign-off) that maps to invoices/tranches
- A PO template and draft SOW so finance/legal can start vendor onboarding
- Clarification on billing: marketplace invoice vs. direct vendor invoice (we have tax/vendor onboarding constraints)

I attached our procurement checklist to this note. Can your team propose a MAP with clear milestone owners and dates? We have a hard fiscal window for commit: PO needs to be issued by 2029-05-10 to hit this quarter.

Any chance we can get a first-cut MAP and PO template early next week?

Regards,
Ian Choi
Head of Procurement, SkyBridge Labs
ian.choi@skybridge.io
SkyBridge Labs

Attachment: SkyBridge_procurement_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Ian Choi <ian.choi@skybridge.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2029 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request + procurement constraints for SkyBridge private offers

Ian — thank you for the checklist and for the call context.

High level: we can support a two-tranche acceptance (tech acceptance then production acceptance) with invoice alignment to each tranche. To get you a usable MAP by early next week we'll need:

1) Confirmation whether you want a single PO that references two acceptance milestones or two separate POs tied to each tranche.
2) Which marketplace(s) to target first — GCP or Azure (we can stage GCP pilot in week 1 and add Azure in week 3 if you prefer).
3) Who is the fiscal approver on your side (name/email) so we can mirror sign-off steps in the MAP.

I've looped in Marissa (billing & enablement) and Karthik (marketplace billing & legal) to draft the MAP and PO/SOW artifacts. Marissa — can you draft a play-by-play MAP (milestones, owners, acceptance criteria) plus a PO template and SOW skeleton that reflect marketplace private-offer flows? Karthik — can you confirm the billing path options and vendor onboarding items we need to surface?

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Ian Choi <ian.choi@skybridge.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2029 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request + procurement constraints for SkyBridge private offers

Ian / Lauren — attaching a first-cut MAP and two supporting docs (PO template + SOW draft). See attachments: redwood-po-template.docx, sow-skybridge-draft.pdf.

Draft MAP highlights (high-level milestones and owners):
- Week 0 (T0): Commercial agreement & PO received — Owner: SkyBridge procurement
- Week 1 (T1): GCP pilot provisioning + tech acceptance criteria executed (smoke tests & latency report) — Owner: SkyBridge SRE / Redwood Enablement
- Week 3 (T2): Azure pilot provisioning (if included) + combined performance acceptance — Owner: SkyBridge SRE / Redwood Enablement
- Week 5 (T3): Production cutover & final acceptance; invoice tranche 2 issued upon final acceptance — Owner: SkyBridge product / Redwood Customer Success

Billing path options to surface in PO template:
A) Marketplace private-offer billing (invoice through cloud marketplace; tax & vendor onboarding handled by cloud provider). Pros: simpler vendor onboarding; Cons: sometimes delayed invoice reconciliation.
B) Direct vendor invoice (Redwood issues invoices directly to SkyBridge). Pros: faster remittance and clearer revenue recognition; Cons: requires vendor onboarding/tax docs earlier.

We recommend option A for initial pilot to avoid vendor onboarding delays, then switch to option B for volume if you prefer. The PO template includes a billing field for chosen path and a drop-in clause for split invoicing (Tranche 1 via marketplace, Tranche 2 direct).

Attachments: redwood-po-template.docx (PO template with billing-path toggles), sow-skybridge-draft.pdf (SOW with acceptance criteria and SLAs).

Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Ian Choi <ian.choi@skybridge.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request + procurement constraints for SkyBridge private offers

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what procurement needed. A few follow-ups from legal/procure:

- Are you able to accept a split billing approach (T1 via GCP marketplace; T2 direct Redwood invoice) as a binding option in the PO? We want that explicitly stated.
- We need Redwood's W-9 and Proof of Insurance (COI) to start vendor onboarding if we pick direct billing for any tranche. Can you attach those?
- Our fiscal approver is Marta Ruiz (marta.ruiz@skybridge.io) — please add her to the MAP so sign-off steps line up with our systems.

PO timeline: we'll prioritize the PO to meet the 2029-05-10 issuance date, but legal needs a final PO + SOW by 2029-04-17 to complete review. Can Redwood commit to that?

Ian

- Redwood: attach W-9 + COI + updated PO template with explicit split-billing clause (Marissa) — due 2029-04-15
- SkyBridge: issue PO referencing DEAL-8412 and indicate chosen billing path per tranche (Ian / Marta) — target 2029-05-10
- Tech acceptance plan & demo for T1: schedule week of 2029-04-22 (Redwood enablement + SkyBridge SRE)
- Final production acceptance: target week of 2029-05-27 (will trigger tranche 2 invoice)

Inline MAP (abridged):
1) 2029-04-15: Redwood sends W-9, COI, and PO (with split-billing clause) — Owner: Marissa Cole
2) 2029-04-22: T1 technical acceptance (GCP pilot) — Owner: SkyBridge SRE / Redwood Enablement
3) 2029-04-24: SkyBridge signs PO + returns to Redwood (if legal approves) — Owner: Marta Ruiz
4) 2029-05-10: PO issued (funding window) — Owner: SkyBridge Procurement
5) 2029-05-27: Final production acceptance; Redwood issues tranche 2 invoice (if direct billing chosen) — Owner: Redwood Finance

I'll attach the W-9 and COI to the updated package and leave the DocuSign link in the final note. If that timeline works, Lauren I'll coordinate a short acceptance demo invite for week of 4/22.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
